title: Drawing two cards from a deck into a hand
description: A deck holds two cards, ace then king. Aldric's Draw button moves the first card of the deck into his hand, twice, in order. The cards are visible to all but Aldric's hand is visible only to him, so a card in the hand is seen by Aldric and not by Bryn; moving a card back out restores all. A third Draw on the empty deck is disabled and its invocation refused.

objects.note: Aldric has hand, a reference to his hand, so owner.hand resolves on the Draw button.
Another character, to show the hand hides its cards from everyone but Aldric.
DESIGN §4.4: a hand is a container visible only to its owner.
The Draw action lives on an object whose cells include deck (a reference to the deck) and owner (Aldric).

expect.note: FIXTURES §9: "A `deck` container with two cards"; ace then king.
FIXTURES §9: "Two Draws, each asserted with `contents` on deck and hand"; before the first, the hand is empty.
"[Draw] when: len(deck.contents) > 0" (FORMULAS §10): the deck has two cards.
FIXTURES §9: "The cards are `visible_to: all`"; the deck does not restrict them, so Bryn sees the ace.
FIXTURES §8: "Every step that is neither rejected nor `bind` appends exactly one group"; no step has run.

steps.note: First Draw: move(first(deck.contents), owner.hand) takes the ace.

expect.note: FORMULAS §10 Draw: "move(first(deck.contents), owner.hand)"; FORMULAS §5: "`first(deck.contents)` draws the top card", so the ace left the deck.
A reference to a container as destination goes into its contents, at the end (FORMULAS §8.2).
FIXTURES §9: each Draw is asserted with "`container` on the card"; the ace is at index 0 of the hand.
The card's own cell never changed (DESIGN §4.4).
A card marked all inside a hand marked to one character is seen only by that character (DESIGN §4.4).
A card marked all inside a hand marked to one character is seen only by that character (DESIGN §4.4).
DESIGN §4.4: effective visibility is "its own `visible_to` intersected with its container's effective visibility"; the king is still in the public deck.
"[Draw] when: len(deck.contents) > 0" (FORMULAS §10): one card left.
An invoke is one group (FIXTURES §8).

steps.note: Second Draw takes the king, now first in the deck.

expect.note: FORMULAS §5: "`first(deck.contents)` draws the top card"; the king was the top card, so the deck is empty.
Draws append to the hand in order (FORMULAS §8.2: at the end).
FIXTURES §9: "`container` on the card"; appended at the end (FORMULAS §8.2), the king is at index 1.
DESIGN §4.4: "A card marked `all` inside a hand marked to one character is seen only by that character"; Aldric is that character.
DESIGN §4.4: "A card marked `all` inside a hand marked to one character is seen only by that character"; Bryn is not that character.
The third Draw: action disabled; len(deck.contents) > 0 is false (FIXTURES §9).
An invoke is one group (FIXTURES §8).

steps.note: The third Draw on the empty deck.

expect.note: Then an invocation rejected with when_false (FIXTURES §9).
A refused step changes nothing (FIXTURES §6).
A refused step changes nothing (FIXTURES §6).
A refused step appends no log group (FIXTURES §6).

steps.note: Aldric plays the ace onto the table.

expect.note: DESIGN §4.1: "Moving an object out of a container onto a board ends the containment"; the ace is on the table at [3, 3].
Moving removes the object from its old container (DESIGN §4.1).
Moving it out of the hand restores all, because the card's own cell never changed (DESIGN §4.4).
DESIGN §4.4: "Moving it out of the hand restores `all`"; Aldric sees it as everyone does.
DESIGN §4.4: "A card marked `all` inside a hand marked to one character is seen only by that character"; the king is still in Aldric's hand.
A move is one group (FIXTURES §8).
